n.story:
Your role is shifting from a traditional craftsman to a 'high-tech artisan.' While your hands still master the tactile manipulation of fine leathers, AI has taken over the tedious mathematical and repetitive aspects of the trade. You no longer spend hours manually grading patterns or calculating material yields; instead, computer vision and CNC cutting systems handle the precision prep work, ensuring zero-waste production. This shift allows you to focus intensely on the 'bespoke' element—the complex problem-solving required for unique orthopedic needs or avant-garde aesthetic requests.

You now act as a creative director for each pair of shoes. Using generative design tools, you can instantly visualize dozens of material and style combinations for a client, simulating how different leathers will age or perform under stress. Your value lies in your ability to interpret a client's vague desires into a technical reality, using AI to bridge the gap between a conceptual sketch and a perfectly engineered physical product. The workshop is quieter and more efficient, leaving you more time for the high-touch assembly and finishing that machines still cannot replicate.
